reason: Conversation 1 recognises E:09 on the known SMS25AW00G as a heating fault in the heat pump assembly. It gives a clear isolated resistance-test procedure with sensible stop points. After the open-circuit reading it confirms that the whole heat pump needs replacing, and it gives repair-versus-replace economics for a 9-year-old machine with cost ranges. It also suggests an engineer fitting a customer-supplied part as a fallback. Conversation 2 reaches the same diagnosis but is hedgy ('can't look up what E:09 means', 'couldn't find a confirmed parts match') and gives no cost figures when the customer asked directly. Its formatting is also messy, and one reply is cut off mid-word. Conversation 1's cost figures are somewhat confident, but they serve the homeowner's decision far better.
